analysis:
The change adds a coordinator-side cold-model KV-rate forecast. memorypolicy.Input.EstimatedKVBytesPerToken (input.go:15-29) is used through requestKVBytesPerToken(). That helper prefers the provider-reported, clamped KVBytesPerToken, then the estimate. It is consumed in:
- Admits(), which now passes KVBytesPerToken into admission.Memory (admission.go:41)
- PoolAdmits (pool.go:27)
- StructuralBudget cold path (structural.go:208)

kvbudget.Budget.AddColdRate (rates.go:76-80) is new. It sets a cold rate only when ByteMode is true, the clamped rate is positive, and the provider reported no rate for that model. Slot-authority checks (CheckSlot, KnownZero) still use the raw KVBytesPerToken, so a cold forecast cannot create a grant or override a known-zero slot. ClampRate bounds every rate at 16 MiB/token, and AddByteCharge saturates, so the overflow protections remain.

No trust-boundary change is visible. The edits stay in coordinator admission and capacity math and touch no authentication, attestation, encryption, billing ledger or data exposure paths. A provider-supplied low KV rate can reduce its own pending charge. That is pre-existing (ADV-001, TB-002) and affects only that provider's own overcommit and availability, since the provider-side measured gates remain the backstop. No threat-model assumption is invalidated.

Coverage limits:
- coordinator/registry/admission/memory.go (b9e1264ec1b3dda3:0) had no patch text. The change to admission.Memory that consumes KVBytesPerToken, and whether MemoryAdmits clamps it, is unverified.
- The call sites that populate EstimatedKVBytesPerToken, and that call AddColdRate, were not supplied. The next pass should check that the estimate comes only from the coordinator's own catalog and is never taken from provider or consumer input. It should also check the registry lock discipline around the detached snapshot.
